ety.text: From Middle English asken, axen, from Old English āscian, from Proto-West Germanic *aiskōn, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eys- (“to wish; request”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian aaskje (“to ask, demand, require”), West Frisian easkje (“to ask, demand, require”), Dutch eisen (“to demand, require”), German heischen (“to ask, request, implore”), Russian иска́ть (iskátʹ), Sanskrit इच्छति (iccháti) (whence Hindi ईछना (īchnā).

From Middle English aske, arske, ascre, from Old English āþexe (“lizard, newt”), from Proto-West Germanic *agiþahsijā (“lizard”), a compound of *agiz (“snake, lizard”) + *þahsuz (“badger”). Cognate of German Echse (“lizard”).

senses.d: To request (information, or an answer to a question).
ex: I didn't know the answer so I asked.

senses.d: To request or enquire of (a person).
ex: I’m going to ask this lady (for) directions.

senses.d: To request (an item or service) (see also ask for).
ex: to ask for a second helping at dinner
to ask for help with homework
Emma asked Jim to close his eyes.
She asked to see the doctor.
Did you ask to use the car?

senses.d: To put forward (a question) to be answered.
To require, demand, claim, or expect, whether by way of remuneration or return, or as a matter of necessity.
ex: What price are you asking for the house?
It’s asking a lot of this old car to make it all the way up to Scotland.
Don’t ask them to the wedding.

senses.d: To indirectly encourage or make more likely (an undesirable outcome).
ex: Walking around with such an expensive watch is asking to be mugged.

senses.d: To publish in church for marriage; said of both the banns and the persons.
An act or instance of asking.
ex: That really does not seem much of an ask.
I know this is a big ask, but …

senses.d: A message sent to a blog on social networking platform Tumblr, which can be publicly posted and replied to by the recipient.
ex: The following example from Black Mental Health illustrates an ask from an anonymous follower seeking social support: […]
He looked at the beast. It was not an eel. It was very like an ask.
